tokyo_kotteri_ramen_sekiyake_s.price_note: PARTIAL: every item named, almost no prices. The shop’s own menu page lists eleven food items, each with a paragraph of the owner’s own description — genuinely informative about how the bowls are built — but it prints a price for only ONE of them, the 餃子 at ¥450, plus a lunchtime 半餃子 at ¥100. Every ramen is therefore recorded with an empty price rather than an invented one. Tabelog could not be checked: as of 2026-09-02 it still returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge body to both curl and WebFetch, so its page for this shop is UNVERIFIED rather than empty and its URL is deliberately absent from sources. ⚠ TWO USEFUL THINGS THE SHOP STATES OUTRIGHT. First, 半ライス無料！！おかわりもっ！！ — HALF A BOWL OF RICE IS FREE, and refillable. Plain rice is the one thing in a ramen shop that carries no wheat, so a coeliac accompanying other people here has something to eat that costs nothing, which is worth knowing even though it is not a meal. Second, the shop descends from なりたけ (なりたけから独立) and its miso tare is 秘伝 inherited from there. ⚠ THAT MISO IS THE HIDDEN QUESTION ON THIS MENU. Six of the eleven items are miso bowls, and Japanese miso is frequently 麦味噌 — fermented on BARLEY. 麦 is not on Japan’s statutory allergen list, so a barley miso is never declared as an allergen anywhere in this country, and a 秘伝 recipe is by definition one the shop will not break down. ⚠ AND ONE NOODLE DESCRIPTION IS WORTH READING TWICE: the あっさり中華そば uses 全粒粉入の細麺 — noodles made with WHOLEMEAL flour. 全粒粉 reads as the health-conscious choice and is sometimes mistaken for a grain swap; it is wheat, milled whole. This is the shop’s lighter bowl and it is no better for a coeliac than the heavy ones. Nothing on this menu suits a vegan: the style is pork back fat, the chashu is house-made, and even the noodles are wheat.

items.note: The shop’s starting point — a clear soup under heavy back fat, ザックザク spring onion and bean sprouts, seasoned a touch strong. This is the bowl whose description carries the 半ライス無料 note. ⚠ Ramen noodles are WHEAT with かん水, and the tare is soy — two wheat sources before any topping. The bowl is finished with 背脂, PORK BACK FAT, which is the shop’s whole style.

The bowl is finished with 背脂, PORK BACK FAT, which is the shop’s whole style.

⚠ TSUKEMEN CONCENTRATES THE PROBLEM RATHER THAN SEPARATING IT: the noodles come dry and the soy tare comes in its own bowl, which can read as more controllable, but the dip is a REDUCED, concentrated soy broth and the noodles are 平打ちの中太麺 — flat medium-thick WHEAT. Portions are 200g, 300g or 400g, or 600g with the large-size ticket; スープ割 (broth to thin the dip at the end) is available on request. The bowl is finished with 背脂, PORK BACK FAT, which is the shop’s whole style.

⚠ THE ONLY PRICED ITEM ON THE MENU, AND ITS DESCRIPTION IS A TRAP WORTH READING CAREFULLY. The shop says 下味が強めについてますので、醤油を付けずにそのまま召し上がってみて下さい — they are seasoned strongly enough to eat WITHOUT dipping them in soy sauce. Skipping the dish of soy at the table feels like removing the wheat, and it does not: the GYOZA WRAPPER is wheat flour, and the 下味 already in the filling is itself soy-based. At lunchtime a half portion is ¥100.

⚠ TWO MISREADINGS IN ONE ITEM NAME. 中華そば means RAMEN, not buckwheat soba — the そば is historical, not an ingredient. And the shop specifies 全粒粉入の細麺, thin noodles made with WHOLEMEAL flour, which reads as the healthy option and is simply wheat milled whole. The lightest bowl on the board is no safer than the heaviest. The chashu here is 肩ロース, leaner shoulder loin, cooked soft.

tokyo_toriyaki_hajime.price_note: No dish and no price, and this is an honest empty reached the hard way rather than by giving up early. The shop has its own site and its own menu page, and that page links two PDFs — menu.pdf (880KB) and drink.pdf (735KB). Both were downloaded and both were extracted. ⚠ THEY HAVE A TEXT LAYER AND IT IS STILL UNUSABLE, which is a different failure from a scan and worth recording precisely: the Japanese characters do not survive extraction at all. What comes out of an 880KB food menu is 483 non-whitespace characters, consisting of the postcode 101-0061, the street number 2-18-2, the phone and fax number 03-3288-0031, the email, the URL, and the opening hours 11:30–14:00 / 17:00–23:00 — every ASCII character on the page and not one dish. The rest of the file renders as dotted leader lines, the row of dots that runs between a dish name and its price on a printed menu, which is the shape of the menu with all of its content removed. The prices are laid out as glyphs too and did not come through either. So the menu is published, it is public, it is not a photograph, and it still cannot be read. Nothing has been taken from the shape of it. Tabelog could not be checked: as of 2026-09-02 it still returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge body to both curl and WebFetch, so its page for this shop is UNVERIFIED rather than empty and its URL is deliberately absent from sources. ⚠ WHAT THE HTML PAGE ITSELF STATES: dinner only, 月〜土 17:00–23:00, closed Sundays and public holidays, 11 counter seats and 12 at tables — a small counter shop. The PDF’s hours line suggests a lunch service too, and the site has a separate lunch.html, so the two disagree; the HTML menu page is the more recently maintained of the two and is what is recorded here. ⚠ ORIENTATION ONLY, since nothing about this kitchen is sourced: とり焼 is chicken grilling, and the one question that decides a yakitori order for a coeliac is タレ or 塩 — a tare glaze is soy sauce, mirin and sugar and is painted on during cooking, while 塩 is salt. Salt-grilled skewers are the standard route, but whether this shop offers each skewer both ways is exactly what an unreadable menu cannot say. Re-check if the shop ever republishes the menu as HTML.

tokyo_brisk_stand_suidobashi.price_note: Full menu with prices, read from the shop’s own official site and the complete menu listing it links to — burgers, sets, toppings, hamburg plates, sides, desserts and the whole drinks list. The listing states there is no course menu, no lunch menu and no takeaway menu. Tabelog was not consulted: as of 2026-09-03 it returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge, so its page is unverified rather than empty and its URL is absent from sources. Many items are marked 水道橋限定, exclusive to this branch. ⚠ A BURGER BAR IS A CLOSED DOOR FOR A COELIAC AND THIS ONE OFFERS NO GLUTEN-FREE BUN, so that is stated plainly rather than worked around. What makes the record worth reading is the SECOND wheat source, which this shop prints in its own item names and which almost nobody reads as an ingredient: eleven of the burgers are listed as 生わさび醤油付き — served with fresh wasabi and SOY SAUCE. Someone who has already accepted they cannot eat the bun, or who orders a patty without one, is still being handed a dip brewed with wheat. The 生 in 生わさび refers to the wasabi being fresh rather than tubed; it says nothing about the soy. ⚠ AND THE FRYER IS SHARED AND DEMONSTRABLY SO. This kitchen fries battered ONION RINGS and battered FISH AND CHIPS alongside its 生ポテトチップス and ポテトフライ, all on the same branch-exclusive side menu — so the chips are a shared-oil problem, not a maybe. ⚠ FOR A VEGAN THERE IS NOTHING ON THE FOOD MENU AT ALL: every burger is beef or chicken, the hamburg plates are beef, the salads are dressed and one is a Cobb, and the only meat-free items are the pickles and the potato sides. The drinks list has one specific trap worth naming — カルピス, in the sour, the water and the soda, is a FERMENTED MILK concentrate. It reads as a soft drink and it is dairy.

tokyo_raoma_hinabebou.price_note: Full hotpot and à la carte menus with prices, tax included, read from the shop’s own site. The course and drinks pages exist and are not itemised here. A TABLE CHARGE of ¥423 per person applies, and there is a two-hour limit when busy. Tabelog was not consulted: as of 2026-09-03 it returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge, so its page is unverified rather than empty and its URL is absent from sources. 渋谷; the shop states 国産野菜 常時40種類以上, 肉10種類以上, ラム肉 部位別に4種類, つけダレ約30種類, and that heat is chosen at the table from 0 to 5. ⚠ THIS IS PROBABLY THE STRONGEST VENUE IN THE TOKYO SET FOR A VEGAN, AND FOR AN UNUSUAL STRUCTURAL REASON: at a hotpot restaurant the customer assembles the meal from individually priced RAW INGREDIENTS. Nine leafy vegetables, ten roots, sixteen mushrooms, tofu in five forms, yuba, and three kinds of glass noodle are each sold on their own. Nobody has to ask the kitchen to leave anything out, because nothing is combined until it reaches the table. A plant-eater can build a genuinely large meal here from the menu as printed, which is true of almost nothing else in this dataset. ⚠ AND THE WHOLE THING TURNS ON ONE UNANSWERED QUESTION: THE BROTH. The shop advertises 無添加・無着色 and a 薬膳 medicinal base, but 無添加 is a claim about additives — it is not an allergen claim and not a vegan one, exactly like the 化学調味料不使用 claim at 叶屋 elsewhere in this dataset. Nothing published says whether the stock is built on chicken or pork bones, and a Sichuan 麻辣 base is conventionally made with beef tallow. Since every ingredient below is cooked in that pot, one question at the counter decides the entire menu — ask it before ordering anything. The shop offers a single-person pot at ¥2,200, which is the practical way to get a broth of your own. ⚠ THE GLASS NOODLES ARE A REAL FIND. Where a hotpot 〆 is normally 中華麺 — wheat — this shop also sells 緑豆春雨 (MUNG BEAN), さつまいも春雨 and さつまいも板春雨 (SWEET POTATO), all naturally wheat-free, plus 豆腐干絲, shredded dried tofu, which works as a noodle too. So the finisher, usually the moment a coeliac has to stop eating, is available here in three wheat-free forms. ⚠ ON THE ~30 DIPPING SAUCES, THE SPLIT IS SHARP AND WORTH LEARNING. Anything ending in 醬 — 麻辣醬, 生姜醬, 香辣醬, 辣椒醬, 沙茶醬, にら醬, 芝麻醬 — is a fermented paste, and Chinese fermented pastes are normally made with WHEAT FLOUR; the same goes for the house ごまだれ, which is sesame loosened with soy. But the shop also sells single condiments: ごま油 ¥121, 一味唐辛子 ¥121, 粉山椒 ¥330, おろしニンニク ¥220, 長葱みじん ¥220, 香菜 ¥385 and four vinegars. Sesame oil, chilli, sanshō, garlic, spring onion and coriander make a complete Sichuan dip with no wheat and nothing animal in it. ⚠ ONE SAUCE IS A SPECIFIC VEGAN TRAP: 沙茶醬 (sacha) is built on DRIED SHRIMP and dried fish despite reading as a bean paste. And 腐乳, which sounds like an animal product, is fermented BEAN CURD and is plant.

items.note: ⚠ THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT ITEM ON THIS MENU, BECAUSE EVERYTHING ELSE IS COOKED IN IT. The shop describes its soup as 無添加・無着色 and 薬膳 — additive-free, uncoloured, medicinal — and that is a purity claim, not an allergen or animal one. Nothing published states whether the stock is chicken, pork or vegetable, and a Sichuan 麻辣 base conventionally starts with beef tallow. Heat is selected at the table from 0 to 5, finished in front of you. Ask what the broth is made of first; every other flag on this record depends on the answer.
The two-person pot. Same broth question.

⚠ THE PRACTICAL ANSWER TO EATING HERE ON A RESTRICTED DIET: your own pot, so nothing anyone else orders goes into your broth. At a shared hotpot the table decides what has been in the water; this removes that entirely, and at ¥2,200 it is the cheapest base on the menu.

items.note: ⚠ THE ONE NOODLE HERE TO AVOID, and the default finisher everywhere else. Chinese noodles are wheat with かん水. The 春雨 above are the substitute, at similar money.

items.ja: 豆腐干絲(トウフガンスー)
items.en: Shredded dried tofu, as a finisher
items.section: 〆・麺・ご飯 Finishers, noodles & rice
items.note: Listed again as a finisher — dried tofu shredded to noodle width. Soy, no wheat.

items.section: 〆・麺・ご飯 Finishers, noodles & rice
items.note: Plain steamed rice.

items.section: 〆・麺・ご飯 Finishers, noodles & rice
items.note: A small bowl of plain rice.
Ōyama chicken under a Sichuan sauce of soy, chilli oil and vinegar.
The smaller portion; soy-based sauce.

items.en: Steamed chicken with spring onion sauce
items.note: Steamed rather than fried, with a scallion-oil dressing — a lighter build than the yodaredori, though soy is usually in the sauce.

items.ja: 白木耳(シロキクラゲ)の和え物
items.note: Snow fungus is plant and this is one of the genuinely vegan à la carte dishes here. The dressing on a Chinese 和え物 is soy and vinegar, which is where the wheat sits — worth asking whether it can be dressed with sesame oil and salt.

items.ja: 細切り豆腐と香菜(シャンツァイ)の和え物
items.romaji: hosogiri tōfu to shantsai no aemono
items.note: Dried tofu shreds and coriander — plant throughout, and the second vegan à la carte dish. Again the dressing is the soy question.
Smashed cucumber with chilli and garlic — plant, dressed with soy and vinegar.
Sliced cold tomato; nothing is published about what comes with it.
Zha cai is pickled mustard stem — plant. Commercial zha cai is often finished with soy and sesame oil.
Jellyfish is animal; the dressing is soy and vinegar.
Chicken under a sesame sauce built on soy.

⚠ AN INTERESTING NEAR-MISS: prawn crackers are made from TAPIOCA or potato starch rather than flour, so they are one of the few crisp things in this dataset without wheat by construction. They are still PRAWN, and they come out of a fryer whose other contents are not published.

items.ja: 麻辣(マーラー)エビせんべい
items.note: As above with a mala seasoning, which may carry a fermented paste.
A preserved duck EGG. No wheat.
Raw cucumber with a miso dip — the vegetable is plant and the MISO is the wheat-or-barley question, since Japanese miso is fermented on koji and often 麦味噌.
As above with cabbage.
Cold tofu — plant — under a Chinese dressing that is soy-based and may carry preserved vegetable or dried shrimp.

items.ja: 揚げ茄子の油淋(ユーリン)ソース
items.note: Aubergine is plant; a 油淋 sauce is soy, vinegar and spring onion, and the aubergine is deep-fried in oil shared with the dumplings and spring rolls.

⚠ THE BEST HOT VEGAN CANDIDATE ON THE À LA CARTE MENU, for one character: 塩. Salt-fried rather than soy-fried removes the obvious wheat route. It stays an ask on both counts because Chinese salt stir-fries are normally deglazed with 紹興酒 — Shaoxing, which is brewed on a WHEAT ferment — and often built on a chicken stock.

⚠ THE TOFU DISH THAT IS NEITHER VEGAN NOR GLUTEN-FREE. Mapo tofu is defined by 豆板醤, which is fermented WITH WHEAT FLOUR, and the standard recipe contains minced PORK. The word tofu in the name does a great deal of misleading work.
Same wheat-fermented bean paste, same minced meat, with aubergine.

⚠ ONE OF THE CLEANEST HOT DISHES IN THIS ENTIRE DATASET: cabbage and steam. No batter, no stock, no sauce named, no fryer. The gluten flag stays an ask only because nothing is published about what it is dressed with when it arrives.

items.ja: 揚げ長芋の花椒塩(ホワジャオエン)
items.en: Fried Chinese yam with sanshō salt
items.note: Yam, fried and dusted with Sichuan pepper and SALT rather than sauced — plant throughout, and unusual in being seasoned with a dry spice mix instead of soy. The open questions are whether it is floured before frying and what else shares the oil.

items.ja: 四川風鶏の唐辛子炒め(辣子鶏/ラーズージー)
items.romaji: Shisen-fū tori no tōgarashi itame (lāzi jī)
items.note: Laziji is chicken dusted in starch, fried, then tossed with dried chilli; the seasoning is soy-based and often includes a fermented paste. The most expensive à la carte dish here.

items.ja: 中華風鶏の唐辛子炒め(油淋鶏/ユーリンチー)
items.romaji: chūka-fū tori no tōgarashi itame (yóulín jī)
items.en: Chinese fried chicken with yulin sauce
items.note: Fried chicken under a soy-vinegar-scallion sauce.
Steamed tofu is plant and clean; the ごまだれ poured over it is sesame loosened with SOY, which is the wheat and possibly the dashi.
Wheat wrappers, and the soup inside a xiaolongbao is set with PORK GELATINE.
Har gow wrappers are 澄粉, WHEAT STARCH — translucent, low in protein, and still a wheat product that Japan requires declared as 小麦.
Wheat wrappers; pork.
Spring-roll skins are WHEAT, and this is the item that establishes the fryer carries wheat — which is what leaves the fried aubergine and fried yam as questions.
Wheat wrappers; prawn.

items.ja: 麻辣(マーラー)唐辛子焼売/2個
items.note: Wheat wrappers, and a mala seasoning built on a wheat-fermented paste.

⚠ THE FIND ON THE DESSERT LIST. Annin dōfu is normally set with MILK and often gelatine — this one is made with SOY MILK, which the shop states in the name, so it has a real route to being fully plant as well as wheat-free. The remaining question is the setting agent, since agar is plant and gelatine is not. At ¥220 it is also one of the cheapest items on the menu. It is an ALMOND dish, which is worth flagging separately from the diets.

items.ja: 白木耳(シロキクラゲ)豆乳杏仁豆腐
items.en: Soy milk almond tofu with snow fungus
items.note: The same with snow fungus, itself a plant. Same setting-agent question; almond.

items.ja: 烏龍茶のアイスクリーム
items.note: Dairy.

items.ja: 揚げたて胡麻団子/1個（ごまあん）
items.en: Fresh-fried sesame ball, sesame paste filling
items.note: Glutinous RICE flour rolled in sesame and fried — no wheat of its own and no animal ingredient in the traditional recipe, which makes this a genuine near-miss. Both flags stay open because of the shared fryer, which this menu shows also cooks spring rolls, and because bean pastes are occasionally enriched with lard.

items.ja: 揚げたて胡麻団子/1個（こしあん）
items.en: Fresh-fried sesame ball, smooth red bean
items.note: こしあん is strained azuki, sugar and water — plant. Same rice-flour shell and same shared fryer.

items.ja: 蒸籠蒸し桃饅頭(モモマンジュウ)/1個
items.note: ⚠ A 饅頭 IS A WHEAT BUN — steamed rather than baked, but flour all the same, which separates it from the rice-flour sweets beside it on the same list.

Tangyuan are glutinous RICE flour balls boiled in syrup — wheat-free by construction and normally plant. The filling is not described, and a sesame or peanut filling is plant while a lard-enriched one is not.

tokyo_shibuya_khao_man_gai.price_note: NO PRICES, ONE DISH — and yet this is one of the more useful records in the set, because of what the shop writes about its own ingredients. 渋谷カオマンガイ is a カオマンガイ専門店, a single-dish shop, and its site carries no priced menu: the only menu links it offers go to Demae-can delivery pages, which were attempted and did not respond at all (connection failure, no HTTP status), so nothing has been taken from them. Tabelog was not consulted: as of 2026-09-03 it returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge, so its page is unverified rather than empty and its URL is absent from sources. The shop runs delivery-only branches elsewhere and a related gapao brand, ガパオガイ, neither of which is this record. ⚠ WHY THIS MATTERS OUT OF PROPORTION TO ITS ONE ITEM: KHAO MAN GAI IS THE DISH MOST OFTEN RECOMMENDED TO COELIACS IN THAI FOOD. Poached chicken on rice with a bowl of clear broth has no noodle, no batter, no fryer and no obvious sauce — it is the standard answer to "what can I eat at a Thai place", and it is repeated in guidebooks and forums constantly. This shop describes exactly how it makes each of the three components, and two of the three descriptions close the door. ⚠ FIRST, THE RICE IS NOT NEUTRAL. The shop writes: 鶏肉をゆでたときにできたチキンスープで炊きあげることで、うまみたっぷりのごはんになります — the jasmine rice is COOKED IN THE CHICKEN STOCK. That is the entire point of the dish and it is also the reason a vegan cannot order "just the rice". A plate of rice and vegetables at this shop is still made of chicken. ⚠ SECOND, THE SAUCE IS SOY, AND THE SHOP SAYS SO. Its description of the 特製ソース is 「タイの味噌、醤油、黒酢醤油を混ぜ合わせ発酵させる事で独特の深みを追求」 — Thai miso, SOY SAUCE and black-vinegar SOY SAUCE, blended and fermented together, with garlic, ginger and chilli. Three fermented soy products in one sauce, and Japanese soy sauce is brewed with WHEAT. The sauce is not a condiment on the side here; it is what the shop presents as the thing it researched and got right. ⚠ THIRD, THE ONE COMPONENT THAT DOES SURVIVE: the chicken itself is 国産ハーブ鶏 simmered gently in water — poached meat and nothing else — and the soup served alongside is described as チキンスープをベースにした塩味のオリジナルスープ, seasoned with SALT rather than soy. So a coeliac who asks for the chicken and the broth without the sauce, and accepts that the rice is cooked in stock rather than water, has a real meal here. That is a conversation worth having at the counter, and it is a different conversation from the one this dish’s reputation would suggest.

items.en: Khao man gai — poached chicken with rice
items.section: カオマンガイ Khao man gai
items.note: ⚠ THE SAUCE IS THE WHEAT, AND THE SHOP NAMES ITS INGREDIENTS ITSELF: タイの味噌、醤油、黒酢醤油 — Thai miso, soy sauce and black-vinegar soy sauce, fermented together — so the signature sauce is three soy products deep, and Japanese soy sauce is brewed with wheat. ⚠ THE RICE IS THE ANIMAL PART: the shop states the jasmine rice is 鶏肉をゆでたときにできたチキンスープで炊きあげる, cooked in the chicken stock, so there is no version of this plate that is plant-based even without the meat. What is clean is the chicken — 国産ハーブ鶏 poached in water — and the accompanying soup, which the shop describes as 塩味, salt-seasoned, rather than soy. Ask for it without the sauce. No price is published anywhere on the shop’s site, so the field is empty rather than guessed.
